title: Spin-orbit-induced gauge field and spin Hall effects in quasi-paraxial fluids of light
abstract: We show that quasi-paraxial fluids of light propagating in nonlinear Kerr media naturally experience an effective gauge field arising from the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction of light encoded in Maxwell equations. By deriving the leading nonparaxial corrections to the nonlinear Schrödinger equation governing the fluid evolution, we find that, for circularly polarized beams, these corrections generate an effective Lorentz force that modifies the fluid dynamics. Remarkably, the corresponding gauge field is not externally imposed but self-consistently generated by the fluid itself, with its sign controlled by the light helicity and its magnitude governed by the spatial variations of the nonlinear refractive index. We illustrate the physical consequences of this gauge field in two configurations: the chiral deformation of normal and superfluid flows past an obstacle, accompanied by a transverse spin Hall force, and the cumulative precession of an optical wave packet trapped in a focusing fluid.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that the spin-orbit interaction in light propagating through nonlinear media generates an effective, self-consistent gauge field. This field acts like a Lorentz force, modifying the fluid dynamics of the light beam. The results predict observable effects such as chiral asymmetries and wave packet precession, connecting quantum optics to condensed matter phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates the effective gauge field and spin Hall effects arising from the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction of light propagating in nonlinear Kerr media.
main_result: The spin-orbit interaction generates a self-consistent effective gauge field that induces an effective Lorentz force, leading to phenomena like chiral deformation and wave packet precession.
method: The analysis involves systematically expanding the governing nonlinear wave equations around the paraxial limit to derive leading nonparaxial corrections.
model_or_system: The physical system is quasi-paraxial fluids of light propagating in nonlinear Kerr media. The dynamics are governed by nonlinear Schrödinger-like equations incorporating spin-orbit coupling effects.
key_observables: Effective gauge field strength, effective Lorentz force, transverse spin Hall force, and the center-of-mass precession trajectory of the optical wave packet.
important_parameters: Light helicity, nonlinearity strength ($g, g'$), and the nonparaxiality parameter ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quasi-paraxial approximation and systematic expansion of the full Maxwell equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the intensity distribution showing chiral asymmetry in the superfluid regime and the precession of the wave packet's center-of-mass trajectory in the presence of SOC.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the full nonlinear wave equation to the paraxial approximation, derives the effective gauge field and Lorentz force, and then applies this framework to model specific physical consequences like flow past an obstacle and wave packet trapping.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics, nonlinear wave physics, and condensed matter concepts (like gauge fields and spin Hall effects) by showing how intrinsic light-matter interactions generate effective quantum mechanical forces.

Intensity distribution δI(x, y)/I0 of a fluid of light flowing past a Gaussian-shaped obstacle at M = 1.36, above the Landau threshold for superfluidity, in the absence (left panel) and presence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) (middle panel, σ = 1; right panel, σ = −1). The intensity distribution is obtained by numerically evaluating Eq. (21). In the absence of the gauge field, it exhibits a characteristic Cherenkov radi- ation pattern, which becomes chiral in its presence: for σ = 1, the intensity is attenuated for y > 0 and enhanced for y < 0, with the opposite behavior for σ = −1. Parameters: R/ξ = 1, q0ξ = 0.96 (M = 1.36), V0/gI0 = 0.2, kξ = 2.

FIG. 2. Intensity distribution of the optical superflow past a Gaussian-shaped obstacle for M = 0.28 (the obstacle is indicated as a dashed circle). Left: intensity perturbation δI(x, y)/I0|σ=1 computed numerically from Eq. (21). Al- though the spin-orbit gauge-field contribution is included, the resulting pattern is dominated by the approximately isotropic depletion around the obstacle. FIG. 3. Transverse spin Hall force Fy/I0 exerted by the fluid on the obstacle due to the spin-orbit gauge field. The force is small but nonzero in the superfluid regime M < 1, and becomes much larger in the normal regime M > 1. The small kink near M ≃1.1 corresponds to the crossover at which the force changes from reactive to dissipative. Parameters: σ = +1, R/ξ = 1, V0/gI0 = 0.05, and kξ = 1.5.

FIG. 4. Trajectory (38) of the probe center of mass in the effective trap created by a quasi-harmonic background beam (schematically represented by the light gray shading). The dotted curve shows the trajectory in the absence of the spin-orbit coupling (SOC), while the solid blue curve shows the trajectory when its effect is taken into account. The solid green curve represents the projection of the latter onto the (x, y) plane, highlighting the precession. Here we chose |ωSO/ωt| = 0.2 and σ = 1.

Spintronics.note: The paper analyzes spin-orbit interaction in optical wave packets, generating an effective gauge field and Lorentz force, which provides a quantum-optical description of spin transport analogous to phenomena studied in spintronics.
